turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Sorry, give me a minute, this computer's crawling again. Mr Naidoo? What did you come in for today?

[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Ja, Ravi Naidoo. I need the form for the new contract at the depot, HR wants it before Friday. I told the sister my knee's been niggling, but that's not why I booked, it's nothing hectic.
[SEG0003] person_1 (DOCTOR): The form, right. The template won't load, so bear with me. Sister flagged your blood pressure out in the passage, I'm just trying to find her note.

[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): She pulled a face, hey. I told her straight it's white coat, soon as I sit in these rooms it shoots up. At Clicks in Umhlanga last month the lady said it was normal, she didn't even blink.
[SEG0005] person_1 (DOCTOR): I'm on her note now. She recorded one hundred and sixty-eight over one hundred and two.
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): No ways. She told me one fifty-four over ninety-six. I repeated it back so I'd remember, because I thought, shame, that's not so bad.
[SEG0007] person_1 (DOCTOR): One fifty-four over what? Say it again, the screen just jumped.
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): Ninety-six on the bottom. One fifty-four over ninety-six. That's what she said out loud to me.
[SEG0009] person_1 (DOCTOR): Ag, okay. The printout on the other tab is a second reading, one seventy-two over one hundred and four. So the file's got two pairs and neither is the one you heard.

[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): Yoh, these machines. My mother's brother had a stroke at fifty-eight, just dropped at a braai, so I do get nervous about pressure. But nobody's ever put me on tablets for it.
[SEG0011] person_1 (DOCTOR): Sorry, who had the stroke? I was still typing the numbers.
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): My mom's brother, my uncle. Only him in the family. My folks are fine, my dad still takes the bakkie down the coast on a Saturday.
[SEG0013] person_1 (DOCTOR): Right. The knee you mentioned to sister. Which one, and how long has it been?

[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): The right one. Since the long weekend when we shifted my brother's fridge, so about three weeks. It aches and it clicks when I take the stairs. Not swollen really, and I still walk the dog round the block.
[SEG0015] person_1 (DOCTOR): Does it lock, or give way under you?
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): Mm, I suppose. Sometimes, not really. It's more just the click.
[SEG0017] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any chest pain today, or shortness of breath?
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): No chest pain, and I'm not short of breath. I had a headache this morning in the queue at the robot on the M4, gone by the time I parked. Otherwise I'm lekker.
[SEG0019] person_1 (DOCTOR): Headache settled, good. Are you taking any tablets, even stuff from the chemist?

[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): Never been given blood pressure tablets. For the knee I take Panado, the five hundreds, two when it's sore. And my wife bought omega capsules at Dischem, big soft ones in a blue bottle, I can't tell you the proper name.
[SEG0021] person_1 (DOCTOR): How often is the Panado? And the omega dose, I didn't catch a number, the cursor's sitting in the dose box.
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): Panado maybe twice a week, only if the knee nags, not on a schedule. The omega, maybe a thousand something, I'm guessing. I take one most mornings.
[SEG0023] person_1 (DOCTOR): A thousand what? Repeat that, there was a noise at the door and I lost it.
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): Ag, scratch that, I was making the number up. I think it's fish oil. One capsule most mornings, except I forget about half the time, so don't write it down as every day.
[SEG0025] person_1 (DOCTOR): Allergies to medicines or food? Penicillin, anything like that?
[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): No, nothing. Prawns, peanuts, I'm fine with the lot.
[SEG0027] person_1 (DOCTOR): Do you smoke, or drink at all?

[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): I stopped smoking when my daughter was born, that's twelve years now. A beer or two at a braai on the weekend, that's it. My neighbour's Weber packed up and he borrowed my grid, whole story, you don't want it.
[SEG0029] person_1 (DOCTOR): Twelve years, and weekends only for the beer. Any diabetes, asthma, heart trouble, or operations?
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): No diabetes, no asthma, no heart trouble. They took my tonsils out when I was small, that's the only one. Appendix is still mine.
[SEG0031] person_1 (DOCTOR): I'll just feel the knee while this thing thinks. Bend it for me. No swelling, it bends fully, and there's a bit of crepitus on the right, which is the click you mean.

[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): Ja, that's it. It's a sore ache, about a four out of ten, worse coming down the stairs, eases once I sit. I'm loading at the depot, on my feet the whole shift, so by lunch it's nagging.

[SEG0033] person_1 (DOCTOR): I'm not starting any blood pressure tablets today. The readings don't agree with each other, or with what you remember. And there's no chest pain or breathlessness with it.
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): Good, I'd rather avoid tablets if I can. The uncle thing still sits in the back of my mind, but if you say we wait, we wait. Should I be checking it at the house?
[SEG0035] person_1 (DOCTOR): It may be white coat, the way you describe it, but I can't properly call it that while the numbers are all over the show. Home readings are what we actually need.
[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): We've maybe still got my dad's old cuff in a cupboard. Or I can pop into Clicks, they're open late, after I fetch my daughter from netball.

[SEG0037] person_1 (DOCTOR): Use a decent cuff, morning and evening, for two weeks. Sit quietly for a few minutes first, write every number down, and bring the list. Nothing from the pharmacy for blood pressure in the meantime.
[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): Morning and evening, two weeks, write them down. And the form, though? HR is on my case already.

[SEG0039] person_1 (DOCTOR): Book back with me in two weeks with that list, and I'll complete the depot form then. No scan for the knee today. If it's still catching you on the stairs when you're back, we'll look at it again.

spec.situation: Patient attends for something minor (a knee or a form) and the nurse finds high BP; BP read aloud twice with different numbers; patient says it is white coat; family history of stroke said in passing; no tablets started today, home monitoring arranged.
features: disputed_numbers: the nurse reads a value and the patient or relative disagrees or remembers another (a dose, a weight, a BP). Keep both and record an uncertainty.
ambiguous_answer: an answer that sounds like yes but is really 'maybe' ('mm, I suppose', 'sometimes, not really'); recorded with uncertainty or not at all, never as a firm fact.
spec.doctor_style: distracted by the computer, asks for repeats

bad.reason: Capsule description and uncertain fish oil supported; frequency overstated because he forgets about half the time.
bad.text: large soft capsules in a blue bottle, called omega, thought to be fish oil (frequency=one capsule most mornings, status=currently_used, reported_by=patient)

bad.reason: Conflict supported, but omits doctor's other file reading 168/102 also not matching patient recall.
bad.text: The patient recalls a blood pressure of 154/96, while the doctor reads 172/104 from the printout and says neither file reading matches what the patient heard. (type=conflicting_statement, related_entities=vital_signs[0]; vital_signs[1]; vital_signs[2], resolution_status=unresolved)

Patient has never been put on blood pressure tablets / is not currently on antihypertensive medication.
Fish oil/omega capsule use is not daily: one capsule most mornings but he forgets about half the time, so should not be recorded as every day.
No medication or food allergies were specifically denied, including penicillin, prawns and peanuts.
Past blood pressure context: patient said a Clicks reading in Umhlanga last month was normal.
Doctor decided not to start blood pressure tablets today because the readings were inconsistent and there was no chest pain or breathlessness.
Plan included no scan for the knee today.
Plan for the knee was to reassess if it is still catching on the stairs at follow-up.
